column3: BootUI checks recorder.hasWrappedDataSource() after SqlTraceDataSourceBeanPostProcessor wraps a Spring DataSource bean; Python has no container DataSource beans, so sharpit treats the SQL source as wrapped once SQLAlchemy statement listeners are attached (or sqlite3 is traced, or an engine is registered on an attached context) and returns "No DataSource has been wrapped for tracing yet." otherwise

Pool connect/checkout/checkin listeners publish ConnectionPayload on checkin with dataSource, waitNanos, statements and obtainedNanos; executed statements pay no per-statement cost; deriving the count at check-in adds about 3.6 µs per released connection (paired sbx measurement, within the 40 µs budget, taken before the overlap tracking, which adds about 0.9 µs per checkout in an in-process timing), growing with the statements on the connection; the count is exact or -1: -1 when the statements since checkout left the SQL Trace ring and the journal, or when the journal's sql events, which carry no connection, cannot be attributed to this checkout (another checkout on the same request and thread overlapped it, a raw sqlite3 statement reached the install, or a statement ran on another request or thread); one gap remains: with no sql journal source, a SQL Trace panel paused for part of a checkout undercounts it

BootUI calls SqlTraceRecorder.registerDataSource only after DataSource proxy wrapping succeeds; sharpit rolls back sqla.add on listener attach failure and requires attached (or explicitly suspended) statement listeners before a registered engine counts as a recorded SQLAlchemy source
